steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Order! Order!

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Answer the question, Young Zoya!

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I already have, Your Honor.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I can't describe what I didn't see. I do not know if Sonya had anything to do with the assassination attempt on the Emperor.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: The committee has heard that you are regularly seen together.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: No, Your Honor.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I have already stated that I did not support them so strongly, and I am no member of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group. As you can see—

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: I know. They did not even give you a badge.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: And, may I ask if the cross-examination proceedings have already begun?

steps.name: Council Parliamentarian
steps.text: According to the bylaws of the 87th Provisional Inquiry Hearing Committee, cross-examination proceedings can only begin once the relevance of all witnesses and evidence has been properly established.

steps.name: Council Parliamentarian
steps.text: Prior to this, the witness may decline to answer questions.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: I have no further questions.

steps.name: Council Parliamentarian
steps.text: Arbiter...?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: ...Young Zoya, I have read your file, and certain things are very plain. For example—

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: You could choose to be a good girl.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Summon the next witness!

steps.name: Council Parliamentarian
steps.text: Summoning Witness No. 2. Witness No. 1, return to your seat.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: You...? Why are you here?

steps.name: Aloof Girl
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: What is your name, Witness No. 2?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Ukusik.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: A strange name.

steps.name: Hearing Committee Member
steps.text: (Whisper) Here are the reference files, Councilor Artyom.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: (Whisper) Orphaned vagrant who grew up on the streets, owing her survival to the protection of the older homeless. They say her de facto guardian died at the hands of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group.

steps.name: Hearing Committee Member
steps.text: (Whisper) She is no friend to the students... I instructed her on what she should and should not say.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Very well. You may speak, Ukusik. No need to be frightened.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: There's nothing to be frightened of... ahem. 'Honored members of the hearing committee.' Did I get that right?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: This is what happened—

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I was selling newspapers on the street corner that night, waiting for Antosha to send someone to take over for me.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Antosha's my boss. I'll talk about him again later—anyway, I saw a bunch of people running to the ballroom, and I was thinking, did something happen to Antosha?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Then a bunch of cops showed up and blocked all the streets. That was when I realized I should have gotten out of there at the first sign of trouble.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I saw one of my pals just standing there blankly while the crowd pushed him around. He yelled something when he saw me—

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: But I couldn't hear what he said before the cop's bashed his head in with a nightstick, and then he disappeared...

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Wait, wait!

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Skip the extraneous details, child... no one knows what you're talking about.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: What am I supposed to say, then? I don't even know how to read, did you think I would talk like a salesman?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: How about you just tell me what to say, and I'll say it?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: No!
The arbiter glares at the noble next to him, who avoids his stare while wiping the sweat from his own forehead.

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Let's start from the beginning. What kind of organization do you belong to? Who's this boss you were talking about?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Why were you there that night? Tell us everything that you know. Conceal nothing.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Everything?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: Yes, everything.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: That's gonna take a while. Can I sit down?

steps.name: Arbiter
steps.text: No!

a.text: Start at the beginning, the beginning... where's the beginning?
From when I was born? Nothing to talk about there. My mom gave birth to me, then she died because she couldn't afford medicine.
The dad who abandoned me? There's even less to talk about. I barely remember him.
Getting drafted into the pipe cleaners, watching other three or four year-old kids like me die in the energy pipelines...
Oh, I can't talk about that? I thought it was legal.
Fine, fine, I guess I'll start with the day I met Antosha...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, can I go home now? You've kept me locked up for so long, my parents are gonna be worried. They can tell you that I've always been a good girl!

steps.name: Lazy Police
steps.text: But today is Monday.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: What's Monday got to do with it?

steps.name: Lazy Police
steps.text: Good kids are in school on Mondays, not stealing on the streets.

steps.name: Lazy Police
steps.text: Let me see... three hours until school's done. Your parents won't be worried. No rush.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Let me out, you svoloch!
Hah, look at 'em.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Who are you laughing at?

steps.name: Jailed Worker
steps.text: Me? I'm not laughing...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Get lost, I'm not talking about you! You over there, kid, what are you laughing at?

steps.name: Jailed Student
steps.text: I'm laughing at him. Look—
I followed the student's gaze and saw the lazy cop looking down at a pie, like he wasn't sure what to do.
It was almost teatime. If he filled his belly now, he wouldn't be able to enjoy the cookies fresh out of the oven at the crossroads.
But the pie filled with fruit and cream looked really good. My mouth was watering just seeing it. I didn't understand—

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: What's so funny about that?

steps.name: Jailed Student
steps.text: Come closer and I'll tell you—

steps.name: Jailed Student
steps.text: He won't get to enjoy his pie at all, if he hesitates any longer.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Jailed Student
steps.text: Wanna bet? You're shaking your head? Don't have the guts? Hah, just you wait...
I didn't believe him at all. I don't make bets unless I've got a sure thing.
I saw the cop look check the time—the head cop would be back soon, and then he wouldn't get to enjoy his pie at all.
So he opened his mouth...

steps.name: Jailed Student
steps.text: Antosha! I'm here!
Antosha nodded at the student, then took out the cop clean and easy. He found the keys on the cop and gave it to the student.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Hurry. They'll be here soon to check the noise.

steps.name: Jailed Student
steps.text: How was I to know that you would use a micro-Originium bomb? Aren't those supposed to be really expensive? How did you get Matvey to agree?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I don't need him to agree to do anything... besides, nothing is more worth more than human life.

steps.name: Jailed Student
steps.text: I thought nothing was more valuable than liberty.
The student's chains dropped to the ground, and he walked out of his cell before punching Antosha in the shoulder. I learned later that's how they show trust and say thank you to each other.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Hey—wait for me! Take me with you!

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Do you know this kid?
The student shook his head. I knew I had to seize the chance, or else those cops would take it out on the rest of us when they came back.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Those men... they're mean to me! I don't have anywhere else to go!

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Not buying that one, huh? Well, you can't just leave me here to die!

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I can do lots of things. I can help—I can tell you're not honest folk, and neither am I!
I heard the sound of a police whistle. It wasn't far. There was no change in Antosha's expression. Normally, that means my words didn't work.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: You're right... we're not 'honest folk'.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Where's home? Maybe I can take you back—

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Home? You mean the sewers of Odoyev? I don't need you to take me there.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Here, the keys. Catch—you know how to open a lock, don't you?
'Course I do.

a.text: Before running from the police station after Antosha, I picked up the pie from the ground. It was mostly clean.
I stuffed it in my mouth as I ran for my life. It was good, really sweet. The cop should've eaten it sooner.
We were going to Katorga.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We can't afford another failure. There are a hundred invalids here, plus the families taking care of them.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Pavlovich's forces keep growing by the day, and their equipment's getting better too. We blast open a way out, they block it again. And our explosives... we've got maybe two shots left.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Only by taking out Pavlovich as soon as possible do we stand a chance of turning this around.

steps.name: Rescued Student
steps.text: Uh-huh.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Did you get a good look at him, Yura? How much security does Pavlovich have?

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Two bodyguards in close company at all times. Anything else is unclear.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We've been planning based on your idea, and—

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I'm done. Gone any more?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Give her the bread basket—look here, remember this face, and find him in Tsarevgrad Raion tomorrow, he'll help you—

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: You got water? I can't get this down...

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Bottle's in the pantry, get it yourself—look at me, not her! The ball's a few weeks away. Do your job and don't get caught. You understand me?

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: I'll be fine. It's not the first time I've worked as a waiter at a ball.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: This is the Winter Ball. You might be the nimblest amongst us, but you need to cut that absent-mindedness out if you want to get things done.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Who are you calling absent-minded? Besides, we pick the pockets of the rich and sell unattended bicycles every day.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Do you write your three or four daily love letters to the same person?

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Come on, Antosha, you're no fun. The redistribution of wealth is serious work, but that doesn't mean everyone has to go around as stone-faced as you all the time.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I'm just reminding you that what we're doing is considered a crime by the ruling class, and we're doing it for—

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: For vengeance.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Yes, vengeance. But far more than that.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: The professor was willing to die for us because he believed we can liberate Ursus and usher in a future of freedom... true freedom.
Creak—
I was standing by the wall and gulping from the bottle when the door suddenly opened.
It was a young man, much taller than I am. He looked really tired, but his back was perfectly straight, like it got a bar of steel in it.
He cocked his head questioningly when he saw me drinking from the bottle, but said nothing.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: You're back, Matvey. We left some bread for you—

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: Hey, there's only half a piece left! Who ate the rest?
I said nothing and quietly put the bottle back.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Ahem. I brought the kid back from the police station. I thought...

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: What were you talking about?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Something failed because you underestimated the nobles, but you've learned your lesson for next time. Did I get all that right?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: ...You were talking about killing in front of a little girl?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Killing? Oh, so that's what you were talking about.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We unanimously agreed that we must assassinate the nobles on the list.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: A list that keeps getting longer. I'm not sure which version you're talking about.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: ...I'll stop when Ursus is cleansed of all scum.
Matvey stared silently at Antosha for a long time, then tossed him the bottle that I put back.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Ahem. I don't really mind if you talk about it. People are either alive or dead. Why avoid talking about that?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Oh, for heaven's sake, just shut up!

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: We don't have any spare beds.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Didn't you think about where she was going to sleep before you brought her back?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I can sleep on the floor.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: You heard her. She can sleep on the floor.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Alright, I'll think of something! I should have thought about it before I brought her back!

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: You can sleep in his bed until he figures out something. He can make do with a corner of the workshop.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Fine, whatever you say. Couldn't have built this house without you anyway.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: We can get you something to eat, girl, then we'll take you home once you've rested.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Home? Where?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Matvey, she's—

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Still, you shouldn't be with us.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Why? Because you're all nobles who get to go to school? I never went to school, but there's lots that I can do!

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: We're not the kind of students you're thinking of...

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: (Whisper) Antosha, you know these are dangerous times. We shouldn't—

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I know! You pick pockets too, don't you? I can help, I'm good at it! Well, I did screw up that last time, but still...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Please, I can help, all I ask is a bit of bread, I don't eat much anyway...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I have nowhere else to go.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: ...You heard her, Matvey. She's another one without a home.

steps.name: Yura
steps.text: With her size, she is less likely to be noticed. We could use a backup plan for communicating with the topside.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Alright, listen up. We're sharing our bread with you, but this is not charity, just extending a hand to someone in need—you don't need to live off anyone's charity.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Everyone has a right to live with their heads held high. If someone is unable to live decently through honest labor, the fault does not lie with that person.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Now, let me ask you something.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Do you believe that there will come a day when we bring down the privileged class, when all of us share equal rights in everything?
Honestly, I didn't really understand what he was saying, but he was pretty excited and all I could do was nod.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: You mean... we'll all get to eat bread? Even cake?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: If I get to eat every day, that's great.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Welcome to the Unbound—
It looked like he just remembered he never asked me my name.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: What's your name?

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I don't have a name. 'Kid' isn't a name, right? Or 'Girl'? Well, I'll know you're talking to me, if you call me that.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: You talk like you're always trying to bite.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Ukusik—'little thing that bites'. That's your name!

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: What? I don't—

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Come, Ukusik, let's get you a clean pillow.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I said I don't wanna be called that!

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: I will—never—answer to that!

a.text: Of course, I ended up answering to it. What a strange name.
Maybe it meant they accepted me as one of them.
For the first time, I found a place that wouldn't kick me out.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Is Yura ready?

steps.name: Resolute Girl
steps.text: Yes. I gave him the knife and poison. When the ball begins, he will approach the target with a tray of champagne.

steps.name: Resolute Girl
steps.text: Killing is easy. The hard part is getting away afterwards... knife or poison. Which will he choose?

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: The one that draws more attention.

steps.name: Resolute Girl
steps.text: That's what I would do.

steps.name: Resolute Girl
steps.text: The professor said that simply carrying out justice is not enough...

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: It must be seen by all.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: This is a dangerous mission, but also our best opportunity, given that guests are not permitted to bring their own security into the Winter Ball. Yura... never mind. I trust him.

steps.name: Resolute Girl
steps.text: Have more faith, Antosha. We didn't follow you to watch you hang your head.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: You don't follow me. We all chose to be here of our own accord.

steps.name: Resolute Girl
steps.text: I know. You're not our leader, of course.

steps.name: Resolute Girl
steps.text: But ideals must have direction. It was your idea to come to Katorga to continue the struggle.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: When Pavlovich is dead, we can leave this place together, and our long struggle will be over.

steps.name: Matvey
steps.text: Antosha.
I saw several people walk in. They were the same age as the students, but wearing worker clothes. They were Antosha's friends, gathered here to do something important.
Important things come together to make great things. That's what Antosha told me.
I saw the crowd gather around Antosha, waiting for him to speak. Antosha took a deep breath. The light shined through the window and fell on his chest.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: I see you. My fellow students, my brothers, my comrades.

a.text: I see you as I did the first time we met.
We were gathered around a great man, listening to his teachings.
I see you thinking of the same questions that you did at the time—
How did Ursus come to this?

spans.text: How did Ursus come to this?

a.text: Where will Ursus go?
What can we do?
I can see it in your eyes that you have lost all hope for this country, and I am the same!
We tried. We are not like those incompetent successors who only dream and talk! We tried!
Peaceful means did not work. We paid the price.
Words were too weak to move an empire steeped in rot and decay.
The professor lost his life because of the 'peace' that we chose, giving his life in exchange for ours.
I see you as I saw our comrades through prison bars, as I fought back tears, witnessing his blood on the execution ground—
Blood that flowed for us!
Blood that has long run dry. None of us fear punishment or death.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We want...

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: Liberty.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We need...

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: To destroy.

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We betray the laws that bind us, for they betrayed the people!

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Destroy all the rotten and pointless systems and institutions, for they are beyond repair!

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: Burn them and hang them, and tear it all down for bread and liberty! Only on the ruins of everything that came before can Ursus finally find—

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: Rebirth!

steps.name: Antosha
steps.text: We are the Unbound. We shall be bound no more.
Their voices were stacked one on top of the other, making me dizzy. I stood next to Matvey, the only one who remained quiet throughout.
I didn't really understand the meaning of those words, but I noticed that Antosha looked this way every so often.
He wasn't look at me, of course... it looked like he was after Matvey's approval.
I don't know what kind of agreement they had, but I knew Matvey would tell Antosha if he went wrong.
And then...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: We saw the one we were meeting with—Yura. He was standing in the crowd, looking confused and lost...

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: He didn't manage to kill his target. The plan got interrupted.

steps.name: Ukusik
steps.text: Maybe he was thinking, why were there so many students and police outside the ballroom?

a.text: 'What were they fighting for?'
